title: Can I Have Two Demat Accounts With the Same PAN in India?
summary: Yes, you can hold two or more demat accounts under one PAN, even with the same DP. See what changes, how to check your accounts, and how to trade across two brokers.
body_markdown:
Yes. You can have two or more demat accounts in India under the same PAN. You can open them with the same depository participant (DP) or with different DPs.


Each account can charge its own annual maintenance charge (AMC). A second account can also affect your eligibility for a low-cost Basic Services Demat Account (BSDA).

## Demat Account vs Trading Account: Which One Do You Need Twice?


A demat account holds your shares and other securities electronically. A trading account lets you place buy and sell orders through a broker.


-


A second demat account helps if you want to keep long-term investments separate.


-


To trade options through two brokers, you need a trading account with each broker.


Once you have both broker accounts,[AlgoTest](https://algotest.in/) lets you connect them under one login and send the same strategy to each.


## Can I Open Two Demat Accounts With the Same Broker?


Yes, if your broker is also a DP and offers that facility. NSDL allows more than one demat account in the same name with one DP.


Trading accounts follow a different rule: you can open only one trading account with a given broker. If you only want a second demat account for your investments, ask your existing DP what it offers before opening another brokerage account.


You use the same PAN for each account. If a KYC Registration Agency has already checked your KYC, the new broker or DP can pull up that record. For a new individual demat account, you can name a nominee or formally opt out. Nomination is optional for joint accounts.


## How to Check How Many Demat Accounts You Have


Start with your Consolidated Account Statement (CAS). Search your registered email for “Consolidated Account Statement”, “NSDL CAS” or “CDSL CAS”. Then open the latest statement, look for the DP names and demat account numbers, and count the different accounts.


Mutual fund folios can appear in the same statement, so count those separately.


1.


If you have a CDSL account, open the CDSL CAS portal. The form asks for your PAN, your 16-digit CDSL Beneficial Owner ID (BO ID) and your date of birth, so keep a demat statement handy to find the BO ID.


2.


If you have accounts with both NSDL and CDSL, check the statement from the depository where you opened your earlier account. That depository sends the CAS unless you asked for a change.


3.


If an account is missing or you haven’t received a CAS, check the statements from your broker or DP. Joint holdings are grouped by the first holder’s PAN and the holding pattern.


The CDSL form asks for a BO ID as well as your PAN. If you don’t know your BO ID, check your registered email or a statement from your broker.


You get a CAS every month in which any of your demat accounts or mutual fund folios has a transaction. If nothing changes, the CAS shows your holdings as of the end of March and September.


## What Changes When You Open a Second Demat Account?


Question


What changes


Will I pay maintenance charges twice?


Each DP charges its own AMC, so check both price lists. Your total cost depends on the plans you hold.


Will I lose BSDA eligibility?


Yes, if you are the sole or first holder of two demat accounts across NSDL and CDSL. Being the second holder of someone else’s joint account does not disqualify you by itself, and the holdings-value limit still applies.


Can I apply twice for the same IPO?


No. Submit only one retail application per PAN, since duplicate retail applications through two brokers can be rejected. If you qualify for a reserved category, such as employee reservation, check the offer document.


How are shares matched when I sell?


The first-in, first-out (FIFO) rule applies to each demat account separately. The oldest shares of that stock in the account you sold from count as sold first.


Do I need a second bank account?


No. You can link the same bank account to both, as long as its details match your identity and PAN records.


Here’s how FIFO works across two accounts. Say you bought 20 shares of a company in Account A in January and 10 more in Account B in June. If you sell the 10 shares from Account B, the sale is matched with the June shares, and the January shares stay in Account A.


This is one reason investors keep long-term holdings and short-term buys in separate accounts.


## Why Do Traders Use Two Brokers?


-


Some keep long-term investments at one broker and active trades at another.


-


A second broker can offer a segment, order type, pricing plan or API support for your[algo trading software](https://algotest.in/blog/10-best-algo-trading-software-in-india-2025/) that the first one doesn’t.


-


During an outage at one broker, a second broker gives you a way to place a new trade. An open position at the first broker still has to be managed there.


If cost is your reason, compare the charges for the way you actually trade. Someone holding shares for years and a trader placing many F&O orders can reach different answers, as the brokerage and AMC differences in[Groww vs Zerodha](https://algotest.in/blog/groww-vs-zerodha/) show.

## Can I Use F&O Margin From One Broker at Another?


No. Each broker checks only the funds and eligible collateral in your trading account with that broker. If you[pledge shares for margin](https://algotest.in/blog/nsdl-margin-pledge/) at Broker A, that collateral supports eligible trades only at Broker A.


Take an example. You sell a Nifty call through Broker A and buy a higher-strike call through Broker B. The bought call reduces your overall risk, but Broker A still charges margin on the short call it holds.


To get any spread margin benefit at Broker A, both legs need to be in that trading account. Use the[F&O margin calculator](https://algotest.in/margin-calculator) to estimate the margin for legs you plan to place together.

## Should You Close an Unused Demat Account?


If an account still charges AMC and you no longer need it, ask your DP about closure-cum-transfer. This closes the account and moves eligible holdings to another demat account you own.


-


When the account holders and their order match on both accounts, an eligible closure-cum-transfer can be done without transfer charges. A separate off-market transfer may cost a fee.


-


Moving shares between accounts you own is not a sale.


-


Download your statements and purchase records before you close the account. Your new broker may ask for the original purchase dates and costs to update your buy average.


## Run One Strategy, Not Two Sets of Guesswork


Two accounts work best when each has a clear job, such as one for long-term holdings and one for options trading. Keep all legs of a strategy in the same account and set the quantity you want at each broker. Check margin at both before you place anything.


After you place orders, compare both order books so a partial fill doesn’t leave the accounts out of step. Before you trade live, replay the strategy on past market days to see how it behaves.

### FAQs


#### Can I open two demat accounts with the same DP?


Yes. NSDL allows more than one demat account in the same name with one DP, as long as your DP offers it.


#### How many trading accounts can I have with one broker?


Only one. To trade through two brokers, you need a separate trading account with each.


#### Can I apply for the same IPO from both demat accounts?


No. Submit one retail application per PAN, since duplicate retail applications can be rejected.


#### Will being a joint holder in someone else’s account affect my BSDA?


Not by itself. You lose BSDA eligibility when you are the sole or first holder of two demat accounts.


#### Is moving shares to my other demat account treated as a sale?


No. Moving shares between accounts you own is not a sale, but keep your original purchase dates and costs.


#### Do I need Multi API to connect two different brokers on AlgoTest?


No. Multi API is only for extra connections to the same broker.
